---
title: Chat Realtime Runbook
description: Verify, publish, stop and roll back the Cloudflare Chat realtime Worker.
updatedAt: "2026-11-20"
audience: developers
---

Chat persists messages in Postgres. The `tuturuuu-chat-realtime` Worker delivers
committed events to hibernating WebSockets. The Web API authorizes each
subscription before it issues a short-lived ticket. It signs publish tickets
against the exact request body. See the
[Chat realtime contract](/platform/features/chat-realtime).

## Configuration

| Setting | Owner | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CHAT_REALTIME_URL` | `apps/web` | Approved HTTPS Worker origin. Leave unset during Worker acceptance. |
| `CHAT_REALTIME_TOKEN_SECRET` | `apps/web` and the Worker | Same dedicated HMAC secret with at least 32 characters. Rotate through the release owner and keep it out of command output and artifacts. |
| `CHAT_REALTIME_STOPPED` | Worker | Secret set to `true` to reject connections and publishes. Set to `false` to open ingress. |
| `INBOX` | Worker | `ChatInboxRoom`, one SQLite Durable Object per workspace. |
| `CONVERSATION` | Worker | `ChatConversationRoom`, one SQLite Durable Object per workspace and conversation. |

The Bun sidecar serves local development when the Cloudflare URL is unset.
The Web API returns polling mode in production when the Worker origin or
dedicated secret is unavailable. Setting the Worker origin disables the SSE
proxy and prevents the local Supabase service-key fallback. Enable the origin
after the web and mobile clients pass staging.

## Local verification

From the repository root, run these commands through resource admission.

```sh
ttr resources run -- bun run --cwd packages/realtime test -- src/chat
ttr resources run -- bun run --cwd apps/chat-realtime test
ttr resources run -- bun run --cwd apps/chat-realtime test:runtime
```

The runtime tests launch workerd through the Cloudflare Vite plugin on an
available loopback port, with disposable secrets and isolated SQLite
persistence. The harness stops its child processes and removes its temporary
state. The fixture exercises the Worker and Durable Objects with synthetic
callers. The live-socket stop fixture switches the room binding in process.
Hosted secret rotation, Web API authorization, Supabase and push delivery
require staging checks.

The local ticket probe uses a second Supabase stack so it cannot attach to the
shared `tuturuuu` project. From the repository root:

```sh
bun --conditions=react-server apps/chat-realtime/scripts/probe-ticket-publish.mjs
```

Run it through resource admission. The script writes a temporary project
`chatrtprobe20` with API port 18521, database port 18522, and the rest of that
block through 18529. It copies this repo's migrations, templates, and
seed into that project, seeds one fixture, and starts workerd with a
disposable HMAC secret. The ticket and publish calls
are `createChatRealtimeSubscribeTicket` and `publishChatRealtimeWorkerEvent`.
Membership is the same `private.chat_get_conversation` RPC the ticket route
uses. The probe does not boot Next, so session authentication stays on the
staging workflow below. It prints PASS or FAIL names and removes the temporary
stack and workdir when it finishes.

## Staging qualification

The **Chat Realtime Staging Qualification** workflow is `workflow_dispatch`
only, and only from `main` on `tutur3u/platform`. Store the `QUALIFY_*`
settings as repository secrets. The job fails before any request when one is
unset, and the qualification script prints check names rather than identities,
tokens, origins, or message text. Phases are `live`, `stopped`, and `disabled`.
Do not set `QUALIFY_LOCAL` on that workflow; the local workerd path is the
probe above.

## Artifact and acceptance

1. Use the **Chat Realtime Cloudflare Artifact** workflow at the reviewed source
   SHA. Pin that SHA, the workflow run and attempt, and the artifact ID.
2. Download the tar and its SHA-256 file from the same run. Run
   `sha256sum -c chat-realtime-output.tar.sha256` before extracting. Compare the
   digest with the run summary and inspect the emitted Worker configuration
   under `output/v0/workers/default`.
3. Check the target account, Worker name, SQLite classes, config and existing
   deployment versions. Keep the prior deployment ID for rollback. Only the
   release owner can authorize publication and routing. Use the pinned cf
   toolchain and the approved prebuilt path to publish the verified artifact.
4. Probe `GET /health`, the authenticated `/v1/connect` upgrade and
   `POST /v1/publish` on the approved staging origin. Use disposable test
   identities to confirm the intended audience receives the event and a second
   workspace cannot receive it. Confirm reconnect behavior and the Worker stop
   switch. Enable the Web origin only after the staged client and fallback
   behavior pass, including confirmation on mobile.

The Worker runs on ingress and socket events. It schedules no alarms, retry
queues or crons. Socket counts, frame sizes, frame rates and replay rows are
bounded as documented in the [Chat realtime contract](/platform/features/chat-realtime#cost-bounds-and-stop-fence).
An accepted publish addresses at most two rooms. Each room retains up to 200
event IDs and ignores a duplicate while that event is retained. Connect
throttles, revocations and replay survive Worker restarts. Presence broadcasts
stop after the room budget for the current window. Expiry and revocation
cleanup run during activity, with zero scheduled wakes. Hosted request volume
and account cost require monitoring during acceptance.

## Revocation recovery

Conversation tickets use the workspace recorded on the conversation. The Web
API checks permissions in the workspace where the user opened Chat before it
issues the ticket. Shared direct and group conversations therefore use the
same room when viewed from different personal workspaces.

A leave or archive writes its audit entry in the same Postgres transaction as
the membership change. Immediate publication and recovery use that entry’s ID
and timestamp. Repeated delivery applies the same cutoff. Tickets issued after
the removal and clock-skew allowance can reconnect after the user regains access.

The `chat-realtime-revocations` native Cron Control processor uses the existing
five-minute schedule. It stays off until named in `CRON_CONTROL_ENABLED_JOBS`.
Before enabling it, configure the Cron Control Worker’s `CHAT_REALTIME_URL` and
dedicated `CHAT_REALTIME_TOKEN_SECRET`. It reads the existing private PostgREST
tables using Cron Control’s database binding, and publishes body-bound tickets
to the Chat Worker. Recovery checks the durable job fence and Worker health
before reading Postgres. One invocation scans completed slots within the
Worker's 15-minute event window and leaves time for processing and clock skew.
It takes up to 32 undelivered records newest first, with at most four concurrent
publishes. The job ledger retains up to 96 confirmed audit IDs until they age
out, so later slots can reach older rows and retry failed deliveries. Overflow
is degraded and does not charge the failure budget. Sustained overflow can
outlast the event window.
Archive recovery uses at most two membership reads per archive to notify up to
1,500 members archived in the audit transaction, plus the actor. Cron Control
dispatches this processor once per slot. The Worker deduplicates by audit ID during replay
retention.
The Web API keeps the audit record when delivery fails.

Workspace membership and `view_chat` changes take effect when Web checks the
next ticket request. An existing ticket can still admit its holder until it
expires, up to five minutes for an inbox and 15 minutes for a conversation.
Rooms check expiry before they deliver further frames.

Before enabling the job, verify the read query plan against staging data and
exercise a publish failure followed by recovery with disposable actors. Check
both stop fences, partial delivery, overflow, and old-ticket denial in workerd.
Cron Control and the Web environment require separate deployment acceptance.

## Stop and rollback

- Set the Worker secret `CHAT_REALTIME_STOPPED=true` for an emergency stop.
  `GET /health` must report `stopped: true` and new authenticated upgrades
  and publishes must return `503`. Send a frame on an existing connection
  to verify that the room closes it.
- Unset `CHAT_REALTIME_URL` at `apps/web` to stop Worker ticket minting and
  publishing. Confirm the ticket endpoint returns `enabled: false` and clients
  resume polling. Check that messages sent while stopped appear after refetch.
  Stop `chat-realtime-revocations` through Cron Control to pause recovery too.
- Roll back to the recorded Worker version if the problem is in the emitted
  artifact. Keep the Web origin unset until staging validation passes again.
  Postgres remains authoritative through every step, so rollback requires no
  message migration.
